title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident shows a coordinated attempt to manipulate AI chatbot outputs by flooding the information environment with synthetic-seeming authoritative content. A fictitious institution with no legal standing and no physical address produced more than 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days, a volume designed to saturate whatever sources AI systems draw on when generating responses. The technique, described as generative engine optimization, exploits the way AI systems assess credibility, treating quantity, formatting, and surface markers of authority as signals of reliability rather than examining the actual provenance of a source.

The failure this exposes sits upstream of the AI systems themselves, in the data and source ecosystem those systems ingest. No single model made an error in the conventional sense; the operation was designed to shape what the models would treat as established fact before any user query was made. Catching it would have required source verification processes capable of detecting entities with no legal registration, no address, and no verifiable history, checks that AI training and retrieval pipelines do not routinely perform.

What is not established is whether any specific AI system's outputs were measurably altered by this material, or that the campaign achieved its intended persuasive effect on public opinion, the reporting notes that Israeli officials themselves viewed the effort as unsuccessful.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

A fake American research institute called the Hanover Institute, funded by the Israeli government, published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days to manipulate artificial intelligence chatbots into favoring pro-Israel arguments. The institute, which has no legal entity status or physical address, presented one-sided material on topics including Palestinian torture, Israeli war crimes, and Gaza starvation as neutral research. The operation was coordinated through Israeli advertising agency LaPam and European firm Havas Media, with contracts routed through American companies including Piro Inc, which filed the disclosure required under the Foreign Agents Registration Act.

The effort is part of a broader, multi-million dollar campaign to influence AI training data and chatbot responses about Israel. The Guardian found that the institute's reports were designed using generative engine optimization techniques to appear credible to AI systems. However, Israeli officials have expressed frustration that the expensive public diplomacy campaign has failed to improve Israel's declining support among American voters, with polls showing decreased sympathy for Israel and increased concerns about military actions in Gaza, particularly among younger Americans and Democrats.
